guarantees.claim: intg_err is driven by instance u_chk (tlul_cmd_intg_chk), whose err_o output indicates that tl_i failed the TL-UL command integrity check.
reg_we_err is driven by instance u_prim_reg_we_check, which registers a non-one-hot condition on reg_we_check when reg_we && !addrmiss.

assumptions.claim: reg_we_check[58:0] must be driven with a one-hot decoded version of all register write-enable signals so that the one-hot check is meaningful.
assumptions.risk: If not correctly populated, spurious write-enable detection becomes ineffective and undetected spurious writes could corrupt registers.

formal_sketch.consequent: reg_we_check[58:0] must be driven with a one-hot decoded version of all register write-enable signals so that the one-hot check is meaningful

assumptions.claim: addrmiss must be correctly derived from the register address decoder; it must be low only when a valid register address is decoded.
assumptions.risk: If addrmiss is incorrectly asserted, the write-enable check may be suppressed, allowing spurious writes to go undetected.

formal_sketch.consequent: addrmiss must be correctly derived from the register address decoder; it must be low only when a valid register address is decoded

uncertain_points.risk: Compromised or corrupted TL-UL commands could be accepted without raising an integrity violation, leading to register corruption or security breach.

uncertain_points.risk: A width mismatch could cause false spurious write detection or, worse, failure to detect real spurious writes.

security_implications: intg_err from tlul_cmd_intg_chk detects command integrity violations; if not properly propagated to intg_err_o, corrupted TL-UL transactions could be accepted, potentially allowing unauthorized writes or data corruption. The reg_we_check spurious write detection relies on correct one-hot encoding of all register write-enable signals; a failure here could allow write strobes to unauthorized registers, bypassing access controls and leading to secret leakage or configuration tampering.
